steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which is UTC+1 during standard time and UTC+2 during daylight saving time (CEST). September 30, 2026, falls during daylight saving time in Spain (CEST, UTC+2).

ET (Eastern Time) is UTC-4 during daylight saving time (EDT), which is in effect in September.

So, 5:00 PM EDT (UTC-4) is equivalent to 11:00 PM CEST (UTC+2).

The time difference is 6 hours: Madrid is 6 hours ahead of Eastern Time.

5:00 PM ET + 6 hours = 11:00 PM Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru is in the Peru Time (PET) zone, which is UTC-5 year-round (Peru does not observe daylight saving time).

The deadline is July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC.

Subtracting 5 hours:  
12:00 UTC - 5 hours = 07:00 local time.

So, the deadline in Lima is July 15, 2026, at 7:00 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST (Central European Summer Time) is UTC+2.  
Tokyo is Japan Standard Time (JST), which is UTC+9.  
So Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of CEST.

The deadline is June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST.  
Adding 7 hours: 9:00 + 7 = 16:00 (4:00 PM) in Tokyo.

Thus, the local deadline in Tokyo is June 1, 2026 at 16:00.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PDT (Pacific Daylight Time) is UTC-7. Madrid, Spain is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which is UTC+1 in standard time, but observes Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) during daylight saving time.

October 11, 2026 is during daylight saving time in Europe (CEST, UTC+2), since CEST typically runs from the last Sunday in March to the last Sunday in October. The switch back to CET happens on October 25, 2026, so on October 11, Madrid is still on CEST (UTC+2).

PDT (UTC-7) to CEST (UTC+2) is a 9-hour difference: CEST is 9 hours ahead of PDT.

So, 11:59 PM PDT on October 11, 2026 = 11:59 PM + 9 hours = 8:59 AM on October 12, 2026 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PST (Pacific Standard Time) is UTC-8. Madrid, Spain is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which is UTC+1 during standard time and UTC+2 during daylight saving time (CEST).  

March 3, 2026 is after the start of daylight saving time in Europe (which typically begins on the last Sunday in March). However, in 2026, daylight saving time in the EU starts on **March 29**, so on March 3, 2026, Spain is still on **CET (UTC+1)**, not CEST.

PST (UTC-8) to CET (UTC+1) is a **9-hour difference**.

So, 11:59 PM PST on March 3, 2026 = 11:59 PM + 9 hours = 8:59 AM on March 4, 2026 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET (Central European Time) is UTC+1. Los Angeles is in the Pacific Time Zone, which is UTC-8 during standard time and UTC-7 during daylight saving time.  

February 2, 2026 is during standard time (daylight saving time starts in March in 2026), so Los Angeles is UTC-8.  

CET (UTC+1) to PST (UTC-8) is a 9-hour difference.  

10:00 AM CET = 10:00 - 9 hours = 1:00 AM PST.  

So the deadline is 1:00 AM on February 2, 2026, in Los Angeles.  

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST (Japan Standard Time) is UTC+9.  
Lima, Peru is in the Peru Time zone (PET), which is UTC-5.  
The time difference between JST and PET is 14 hours (9 - (-5) = 14).

So, 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026 is 8:00 - 14 = 18:00 (6:00 PM) on May 4, 2026 in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which is UTC+1 during standard time and UTC+2 during daylight saving time (CEST). October 28, 2026, falls after the end of daylight saving time in Europe (which is typically the last Sunday in October). In 2026, daylight saving time ends on October 25, so on October 28, Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1).

PT (Pacific Time) on October 28, 2026, is PDT (Pacific Daylight Time, UTC-7) because daylight saving time in the U.S. ends on November 1, 2026. So:

- 11:59 PM PT (PDT) = UTC-7
- Convert to UTC: 11:59 PM + 7 hours = 6:59 AM UTC
- Convert to Madrid (CET, UTC+1): 6:59 AM + 1 hour = 7:59 AM

So the deadline in Madrid is 7:59 AM on October 29, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid, Spain is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which is UTC+1. Eastern Time (ET) is UTC-5 during standard time (EST) or UTC-4 during daylight saving time (EDT). October 30, 2026 is after the end of daylight saving time in the U.S. (which ends on the first Sunday in November), so ET will be EST (UTC-5).

Therefore, 9:00 AM ET (UTC-5) = 14:00 UTC.

Madrid is UTC+1, so 14:00 UTC = 15:00 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 15:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET (Central European Time) is UTC+1. New York is in the Eastern Time Zone, which is UTC-5 during standard time and UTC-4 during daylight saving time. October 27, 2026 is after the U.S. daylight saving time ends (which is the first Sunday in November), so on October 27, 2026, New York will be on Eastern Standard Time (EST), UTC-5.

CET (UTC+1) to EST (UTC-5) is a 6-hour difference, with EST being behind CET.

So, 18:00 CET minus 6 hours = 12:00 EST.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 12:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid, Spain is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which is UTC+1 during standard time and UTC+2 during daylight saving time (CEST). November 2, 2026 is after the end of daylight saving time in Europe (which typically ends on the last Sunday of October), so Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1) on that date.

PT (Pacific Time) on November 2, 2026, will be PST (Pacific Standard Time, UTC-8), since Daylight Saving Time ends in the U.S. on the first Sunday of November — which in 2026 is November 1. So on November 2, PT is PST (UTC-8).

The time difference between PST (UTC-8) and CET (UTC+1) is 9 hours. So when it’s 11:59 PM PST on November 2, it’s already 8:59 AM on November 3 in Madrid.

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

However, in 2026, DST in the EU starts on March 29, so on March 20, Madrid is still on CET (UTC+1).

Pacific Time (PT) on March 20, 2026, is Pacific Standard Time (PST, UTC-8), because Daylight Saving Time in the U.S. starts on March 8, 2026, so PT is PDT (UTC-7) by then.

Wait — correction: In 2026, U.S. Daylight Saving Time begins on Sunday, March 8, so by March 20, 2026, the U.S. is on PDT (UTC-7). Madrid, however, is still on CET (UTC+1), because EU DST starts on March 29, 2026.

So:
- Deadline: March 20, 2026, 11:59 PM PDT (UTC-7)
- Convert to Madrid time (CET, UTC+1): Add 8 hours.

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET (Central European Time) is UTC+1. Los Angeles is in the Pacific Time Zone, which is UTC-8 during standard time and UTC-7 during daylight saving time.

March 25, 2026 is after the U.S. daylight saving time start (second Sunday in March), so Los Angeles will be on PDT (UTC-7).

CET (UTC+1) to PDT (UTC-7) is an 8-hour difference. So when it’s 12:00 PM CET, it’s 4:00 AM in Los Angeles.

Thus, 12:00 PM CET on March 25, 2026 = 4:00 AM PDT on the same day.

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

ET (Eastern Time) is UTC-4 during Daylight Saving Time (EDT) and UTC-5 during Standard Time (EST). October 12, 2026, falls after the U.S. Daylight Saving Time ends (which is the first Sunday in November), so on October 12, 2026, the U.S. is still observing EDT (UTC-4).

12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026 = 00:00 UTC-4 → 04:00 UTC.

Madrid is in Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1 in standard time, but observes Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) from late March to late October. October 12, 2026, is still within CEST (since DST ends on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026).

So, 04:00 UTC = 06:00 CEST in Madrid.

Therefore, the deadline is 6:00 AM on October 12, 2026, in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE stands for "Anywhere on Earth," which is the latest time zone on Earth (UTC−12). The deadline is 23:59 AoE on October 9, 2026, meaning it’s still October 9 everywhere on Earth at that moment.

Madrid is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which is UTC+1 during standard time and UTC+2 during daylight saving time (CEST). Spain observes daylight saving time, switching to CEST (UTC+2) on the last Sunday in March and back to CET on the last Sunday in October.

October 9, 2026 is after the last Sunday in October (which is October 25, 2026), so on October 9, 2026, Spain is still on CEST (UTC+2).

Therefore, AoE (UTC−12) is 14 hours behind CEST (UTC+2).

So, 23:59 AoE on October 9 = 23:59 + 14 hours = 13:59 on October 10 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

PT (Pacific Time) in August is PDT (Pacific Daylight Time), which is UTC-7.

So, 12:00 PM PT (PDT) = 12:00 UTC-7.

Convert UTC to Madrid (CEST, UTC+2): 19:00 + 2 = 21:00.

So, 12:00 PM PT on August 14, 2026, is 21:00 CEST on August 14, 2026, in Madrid.

Since the deadline is November 10, 2026 — which is after the end of daylight saving time in Europe (typically last Sunday in October) — Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1).

So, IST (UTC+5:30) is 4 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Madrid (UTC+1).

To convert 11:59 PM IST on November 10, 2026, to Madrid time:

11:59 PM - 4 hours 30 minutes = 7:29 PM on the same day.

Thus, the deadline in Madrid is 7:29 PM CET on November 10, 2026.

Lima, Peru is in the Peru Time (PET) zone, which is UTC-5.  

The time difference between Nepal and Lima is:  
5 hours 45 minutes + 5 hours = 10 hours 45 minutes.  
So Lima is 10 hours 45 minutes behind Nepal.

Deadline in Nepal: April 2, 2026, 5:00 PM NPT  
Subtract 10 hours 45 minutes:

So the deadline in Lima is April 2, 2026, 6:15 AM local time.

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

October 6, 2026 is after the end of daylight saving time in Spain (which typically ends on the last Sunday of October). So on October 6, 2026, Spain will still be on CEST (UTC+2), because daylight saving ends on October 25, 2026.

Adelaide (UTC+9:30) is 7 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Madrid (UTC+2).

So, 10:00 AM Adelaide time on October 6, 2026 is:

10:00 - 7h30m = 02:30 in Madrid.

Therefore, the deadline in Madrid is 02:30 on October 6, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 02:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney, Australia (AEST) is typically 9 hours ahead of Madrid, Spain (CET/CEST). However, we must consider daylight saving time (DST) transitions.

- Madrid observes Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) from late March to late October.
- Sydney observes Australian Eastern Summer Time (AEST becomes AEDT, UTC+11) from early October to early April.

On October 3, 2026:  
- Sydney will still be on AEDT (UTC+11), as DST in Sydney typically ends in early April and starts again in early October — so October 3 is still within DST.  
- Madrid will still be on CEST (UTC+2), since DST ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026), so October 3 is still in CEST.

Thus, Sydney (AEDT, UTC+11) is 9 hours ahead of Madrid (CEST, UTC+2).

So, 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026 = 6:00 PM - 9 hours = 9:00 AM in Madrid.

Therefore, the deadline in Madrid is 9:00 AM on October 3, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 09:00
